status: POST-HOC SENSITIVITY CONTROL, explicitly declared, NOT part of the primary preregistered contrast
trigger: After inspecting the preregistered run, A_plain (no winsorisation at all) produced macro RMSE 1.65-1.93 on scale-sensitive models, with 38/50 Ridge targets above RMSE 1.0 and median 1.4997. The Ridge ladder showed a single fold-wise 1/99% clip (L1) already cuts RMSE from 1.6471 to 0.5026, better than both proposed arms (B_log 0.6606, B_increment 0.5817). A no-protection baseline is therefore a straw man: any routine chemometric workflow applies some outlier handling.
question: Does the chemistry-aware preprocessing have ANY incremental value over a routine pipeline WITH THE SAME outlier protection? This is the stricter, reviewer-relevant comparison.

A_clip.label: Routine preprocessing + fold-wise winsorisation (fair baseline)
A_clip.note: Identical to ladder step L1. z-score plus fold-wise 1/99% clipping, no chemical-unit priors.

models: The SAME 8 registered models with the SAME frozen hyperparameters as prep_h2h_preregistration.json. No model added, removed or retuned.
metrics: Identical to the preregistration: macro RMSE, macro Spearman rho, per-target paired Wilcoxon on 250 OOF squared-error differences, BH-FDR within each (contrast, model).
reporting_rule: All results reported in full regardless of direction. This addendum may OVERTURN the headline 'our method is better' claim and must be reported to the authors verbatim if it does.
honesty_note: Because this arm was added after seeing the primary results, its outcomes are labelled sensitivity/robustness evidence and cannot be presented as a confirmatory preregistered test.
